about: Prevention lines per hazard kind, phase and language. Each line paraphrases the official page in `source`; `quote` is the verbatim excerpt of that page it was written from (checked as a substring of the fetched page text on 2026-10-26). `needs_review` marks a judgement call explained in `note`; the API also flags any line whose source is not in the line's language.

before.text: Secure heavy items like bookcases, water heaters and TVs.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Earthquakes

before.quote: Secure heavy items in your home like bookcases, refrigerators, water heaters, televisions and objects that hang on walls.

before.text: Store heavy and breakable objects on low shelves.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Earthquakes

before.quote: Store heavy and breakable objects on low shelves.

before.text: Practice how to protect yourself during earthquakes.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Earthquakes

before.quote: Practice how to protect yourself during earthquakes

before.text: Make a kit with several days of food, water and a whistle.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Earthquakes

before.quote: Make a supply kit that includes enough food and water for several days, a flashlight, a fire extinguisher and a whistle.

during.text: Drop onto your hands and knees where you are.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Earthquakes

during.quote: Drop where you are onto hands and knees.

during.text: Cover head and neck; crawl under a sturdy table if near.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Earthquakes

during.quote: Cover your head and neck with one arm and hand. If a sturdy table or desk is nearby, crawl underneath it for shelter.

during.text: Hold on until the shaking stops.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Earthquakes

during.quote: Hold until the shaking stops. If under shelter, hold on with one hand and be ready to move with it when the shelter moves.

during.text: Stay inside; do not run outside, and avoid doorways.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Earthquakes

during.quote: If you are inside, stay and do not run outside; avoid doorways.

after.text: Expect aftershocks; Drop, Cover and Hold On when you feel one.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Earthquakes

after.quote: Expect aftershocks to follow the main shock of an earthquake. Be ready to Drop, Cover and Hold On if you feel an aftershock.

after.text: In tsunami zones, go inland or to higher ground immediately.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Earthquakes

after.quote: If you are in an area that may experience tsunamis, go inland or to higher ground immediately after the shaking stops.

after.text: Leave damaged buildings quickly and do not re-enter them.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Earthquakes

after.quote: If you are in a damaged building, go outside and quickly move away from the building. Do not enter damaged buildings.

after.text: If trapped, text, bang on a pipe or use a whistle.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Earthquakes

after.quote: If you are trapped, send a text or bang on a pipe or wall. Cover your mouth with your shirt for protection and instead of shouting, use a whistle.

before.text: Learn tsunami signs: earthquake, ocean roar, sudden rise or draining of water.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Tsunamis

before.quote: Learn the signs of a potential tsunami, such as an earthquake, a loud roar from the ocean, or unusual ocean behavior, such as a sudden rise or wall of water or sudden draining of water showing the ocean floor.

before.text: Know and practice evacuation routes from home, work and play.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Tsunamis

before.quote: Know and practice community evacuation plans. Some at-risk communities have maps with evacuation zones and routes. Map out your routes from home, work and play.

before.text: Pick shelters 100+ feet above sea level or 1+ mile inland.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Tsunamis

before.quote: Pick shelters 100 feet or more above sea level, or at least one mile inland.

before.text: Sign up for your community's warning system.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Tsunamis

before.quote: Sign up for your community’s warning system.

during.text: If an earthquake hits, protect yourself first: Drop, Cover, Hold On.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Tsunamis

during.quote: If there is an earthquake and you are in a tsunami area, protect yourself from the earthquake first. Drop, Cover, and Hold On.

during.text: On any sign or warning, go high and far inland immediately.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Tsunamis

during.quote: When the shaking stops, if there are natural signs or official warnings of a tsunami, move immediately to a safe place as high and as far inland as possible.

during.text: Do not wait for official warnings or evacuation orders.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Tsunamis

during.quote: Listen to the authorities, but do not wait for tsunami warnings and evacuation orders.

during.text: If in the water, grab onto something that floats.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Tsunamis

during.quote: If you are in the water, then grab onto something that floats, such as a raft or tree trunk.

after.text: Stay out of the hazard zone until officials say it is safe.

source.name: National Weather Service (NOAA) -- After a Tsunami

after.quote: Stay out of the tsunami hazard or evacuation zone until local officials tell you it is safe. The cancellation of a tsunami warning does not mean the danger has passed.

after.text: Expect more waves; the first may not be the largest.

source.name: National Weather Service (NOAA) -- During a Tsunami

after.quote: The first wave may not be the last or the largest.

after.text: Avoid floodwater: it can carry debris and be deeper than it looks.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Tsunamis

after.quote: Avoid wading in floodwater, which can contain dangerous debris. Water may be deeper than it appears.

after.text: Stay away from damaged buildings, roads and bridges.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Tsunamis

after.quote: Stay away from damaged buildings, roads and bridges.

before.text: Ask local officials about evacuation, shelter and ash protection plans.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Volcanoes

before.quote: Ask local emergency management for evacuation and shelter plans, and for potential means of protection from ash.

before.text: Sign up for alerts that notify you of volcanic activity.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Volcanoes

before.quote: Learn about community warning systems by signing up for a free service called the Volcano Notification Service (VNS) that sends notifications about volcanic activity.

before.text: Store several days of food, water and cleaning supplies.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Volcanoes

before.quote: including nonperishable foods, cleaning supplies and water for several days, in case you have to evacuate immediately or if services are cut off.

before.text: Consult your doctor if you already have breathing problems.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Volcanoes

before.quote: Consult your doctor if you have existing respiratory difficulties.

during.text: Follow evacuation orders from local authorities and evacuate early.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Volcanoes

during.quote: Follow evacuation orders from local authorities. Evacuate early.

during.text: Avoid areas downwind and river valleys downstream of the volcano.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Volcanoes

during.quote: Avoid areas downwind, and river valleys downstream, of the volcano. Rubble and ash will be carried by wind and gravity.

during.text: Shelter in place from ash; cover vents, seal doors and windows.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Volcanoes

during.quote: Take temporary shelter from volcanic ash in the location where you are, if you have enough supplies. Cover ventilation openings and seal doors and windows.

during.text: If outside, wear a well-fitting certified mask such as an N95.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Volcanoes

during.quote: If outside, protect yourself from falling ash that can irritate skin and injure breathing passages, eyes and open wounds. Use a well-fitting, certified face mask, such as an N95.

after.text: Stay indoors until authorities say it is safe to go outside.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Volcanoes

after.quote: Listen to authorities to find out when it is safe to return after an eruption. Stay indoors until authorities say it is safe to go outside.

after.text: Avoid driving in heavy ash; it can clog engines and stall cars.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Volcanoes

after.quote: Avoid driving in heavy ash. Driving will stir up volcanic ash that can clog engines and stall vehicles.

after.text: Do not climb on your roof for ash without guidance or training.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Volcanoes

after.quote: Do not get on your roof to remove ash unless you have guidance or training. If you have to remove ash, then be very careful as ash makes surfaces slippery.

after.text: Wear protective clothing and a mask when cleaning up.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Volcanoes

after.quote: Wear protective clothing and a mask when cleaning up. Children should not help with cleanup efforts.

before.text: Know if you live in an evacuation zone and learn your routes.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Hurricanes

before.quote: You may have to evacuate quickly due to a hurricane if you live in an evacuation zone. Learn your evacuation routes

before.text: Gather supplies and medication; you may lack access for days or weeks.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Hurricanes

before.quote: Have enough supplies for your household. Include medication, disinfectant supplies and pet supplies in your go bag or car trunk. You may not have access to these supplies for days or even weeks after a hurricane.

before.text: Have several ways to receive alerts.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Hurricanes

before.quote: Be sure to have several ways to receive alerts.

before.text: Clear drains and gutters, bring in outdoor furniture, consider shutters.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Hurricanes

before.quote: De-clutter drains and gutters, bring in outside furniture and consider hurricane shutters.

during.text: Evacuate immediately if local officials tell you to leave.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Hurricanes

during.quote: If you live in a mandatory evacuation zone and local officials tell you to evacuate, do so immediately.

during.text: For high winds, shelter in a storm shelter or interior room.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Hurricanes

during.quote: Take refuge in a designated storm shelter or an interior room for high winds.

during.text: Never walk, swim or drive through flood waters. Turn Around, Don't Drown.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Hurricanes

during.quote: Do not walk, swim or drive through flood waters. Turn Around. Don’t Drown! Just six inches of fast-moving water can knock you down, and one foot of moving water can sweep your vehicle away.

during.text: Trapped by flooding? Go to the highest level, not a closed attic.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Hurricanes

during.quote: Go to the highest level of the building if you are trapped by flooding. Do not climb into a closed attic. You may become trapped by rising flood water.

after.text: Follow local officials for information and special instructions.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Hurricanes

after.quote: Pay attention to local officials for information and special instructions.

after.text: Do not wade in floodwater; it can be contaminated or electrified.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Hurricanes

after.quote: Do not wade in flood water, which can contain dangerous pathogens that cause illnesses. This water also can contain debris, chemicals, waste and wildlife. Underground or downed power lines can electrically charge the water.

after.text: Don't touch electrical equipment if wet or standing in water.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Hurricanes

after.quote: Do not touch electrical equipment if it is wet or if you are standing in water.

after.text: Save calls for emergencies; text or use social media instead.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Hurricanes

after.quote: Save phone calls for emergencies. Phone systems often are down or busy after a disaster. Use text messages or social media to communicate with family and friends.

before.text: Sign up for your community's warning system.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Floods

before.quote: Where it rains it can flood. Sign up for your community’s warning system.

before.text: Learn and practice evacuation routes, shelter plans and flash flood response.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Floods

before.quote: Learn and practice evacuation routes, shelter plans and flash flood response.

before.text: Gather several days of food and water in case you must leave.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Floods

before.quote: Gather supplies, including non-perishable foods, cleaning supplies and water for several days, in case you must leave immediately or if services are cut off in your area.

before.text: Keep important documents in a waterproof container.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Floods

before.quote: In case of emergency, keep documents in a waterproof container.

during.text: Never walk, swim or drive through flood waters. Turn Around, Don't Drown.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Floods

during.quote: Do not walk, swim or drive through flood waters. Turn Around. Don’t Drown!

during.text: Evacuate immediately if told to, and never drive around barricades.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Floods

during.quote: Evacuate immediately, if told to do so. Never drive around barricades.

during.text: Car trapped? Stay inside; get on the roof if water rises inside.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Floods

during.quote: Stay inside your car if it is trapped in rapidly moving water. Get on the roof if water is rising inside the car.

during.text: If trapped inside, go to the highest level, never a closed attic.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Floods

during.quote: Get to the highest level if trapped in a building. Only get on the roof if necessary and once there, signal for help. Do not climb into a closed attic to avoid getting trapped by rising floodwater.

after.text: Return home only when authorities say it is safe.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Floods

after.quote: Pay attention to authorities for information and instructions. Return home only when authorities say it is safe.

after.text: Avoid wading in floodwater; it can be contaminated or electrically charged.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Floods

after.quote: Avoid wading in floodwater, which can be contaminated and contain dangerous debris. Underground or downed power lines can electrically charge the water.

after.text: Use generators only outdoors and away from windows.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Floods

after.quote: Use a generator or other gasoline-powered machinery ONLY outdoors and away from windows.

after.text: Confirm tap water is safe; follow any boil-water advice.

source.name: National Weather Service (NOAA) -- After a Flood

after.quote: Ensure water is safe to drink, cook or clean with after a flood. Authorities may ask you to boil water for a while after a flood.

before.text: Keep at least 30 feet around home clear of leaves and flammables.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Wildfires

before.quote: Create a fire-resistant zone that is free of leaves, debris or flammable materials for at least 30 feet from your home.

before.text: Be ready to evacuate quickly; learn your evacuation routes.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Wildfires

before.quote: You may have to evacuate quickly due to a wildfire. Learn your evacuation routes

before.text: Have several ways to receive alerts.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Wildfires

before.quote: Have several ways to receive alerts.

before.text: Store an N95 mask to protect yourself from smoke.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Wildfires

before.quote: If available, store an N95 mask to protect yourself from smoke inhalation.

during.text: Evacuate immediately if authorities tell you to do so.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Wildfires

during.quote: Evacuate immediately if authorities tell you to do so.

during.text: If trapped, call emergency services, give your location, turn on lights.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Wildfires

during.quote: If trapped, call 9-1-1 and give your location, but be aware that emergency response could be delayed or impossible. Turn on lights to help rescuers find you.
during.note: The page says 9-1-1; generalized to 'emergency services' for users outside the US.

during.text: Use an N95 mask or limit your exposure to smoke.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Wildfires

during.quote: Use an N95 mask to protect yourself from smoke inhalation or limit your exposure to smoke by doing the following:

during.text: If not evacuating, shelter indoors where smoke levels are lower.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Wildfires

during.quote: If you are not ordered to evacuate but smoky conditions exist, stay inside in a safe location or go to a community building where smoke levels are lower.

after.text: Do not return home until authorities say it is safe.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Wildfires

after.quote: Do not return home until authorities say it is safe to do so.

after.text: Avoid hot ash, charred trees, smoldering debris and live embers.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Wildfires

after.quote: Avoid hot ash, charred trees, smoldering debris and live embers. The ground may contain heat pockets that can burn you or spark another fire.

after.text: Use a respirator and wet debris to limit breathing dust.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Wildfires

after.quote: Use a respirator to limit your exposure, and wet debris to minimize breathing dust particles.

after.text: Text or use social media to reach family; call only in emergencies.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Wildfires

after.quote: Send text messages or use social media to reach out to family and friends. Phone systems are often busy following a disaster. Make calls only in emergencies.

before.text: Make conserving water a part of your daily life.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Drought

before.quote: The best way to prepare for a drought is to conserve water. Make conserving water a part of your daily life.

before.text: Check plumbing for leaks and have them repaired.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Drought

before.quote: Check all plumbing for leaks and have any leaks repaired by a plumber.

before.text: Never pour away water that could be reused, such as for plants.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Drought

before.quote: Never pour water down the drain when there may be another use for it. For example, use it to water your indoor plants or garden.

during.text: Always follow state and local water-use restrictions.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Drought

during.quote: Always observe state and local restrictions on water use during a drought. Contact your state or local government for current information and suggestions.

during.text: If officials ask, do not burn brush or trash in dry weather.

source.name: National Weather Service (NOAA) -- Understand Drought and Know How to Respond

during.quote: Dry conditions often lead to brush fires or wildfires. Local officials may ask that you not burn brush or trash during dry conditions and comply with other safety precautions.

during.text: Always follow evacuation orders issued in extreme fire conditions.

source.name: National Weather Service (NOAA) -- Understand Drought and Know How to Respond

during.quote: In extreme fire conditions, officials may issue mandatory evacuation orders to protect your life. Always follow these directives.

during.text: Take short showers instead of baths to save water.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Drought

during.quote: Take short showers instead of baths. Turn on the water only to get wet and lather and then again to rinse off.

after.text: Ask your local water provider for information and assistance.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Drought

after.quote: Contact your local water provider for information and assistance.
after.note: Ready.gov's drought page has no 'after' section. This line comes from its 'Before a Drought' outdoor tips; it is placed in 'after' as preparation for the next dry period. Confirm the phase placement.

after.text: Plant native or drought-tolerant grasses, shrubs and trees.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Drought

after.quote: Plant native and/or drought-tolerant grasses, ground covers, shrubs and trees. Once established, your plants won't need as much watering.
after.note: Ready.gov's drought page has no 'after' section. This line comes from its 'Before a Drought' outdoor tips; it is placed in 'after' as preparation for the next dry period. Confirm the phase placement.

before.text: Sign up for your community's warning system.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Thunderstorms & Lightning

before.quote: Sign up for your community’s warning system. The Emergency Alert System (EAS) and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Weather Radio also provide emergency alerts.

before.text: Pick and practice a tornado shelter: safe room or interior windowless room.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Tornadoes

before.quote: Identify and practice going to a safe shelter such as a safe room built using FEMA criteria or a storm shelter built to ICC 500 standards. The next best protection is a small, interior, windowless room or basement on the lowest level of a sturdy building.

before.text: Identify sturdy buildings near where you live, work, study and play.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Thunderstorms & Lightning

before.quote: Identify sturdy buildings close to where you live, work, study and play.

before.text: Install and test smoke alarms and carbon monoxide detectors.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Winter Weather

before.quote: Install and test smoke alarms and carbon monoxide detectors with battery backups.

before.text: Keep a car kit: flashlight, warm clothes, blankets, water and snacks.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Winter Weather

before.quote: Create an emergency supply kit for your car. Include jumper cables, sand, a flashlight, warm clothes, blankets, bottled water and non-perishable snacks.

during.text: When thunder roars, go indoors, into a building or roofed car.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Thunderstorms & Lightning

during.quote: When thunder roars, go indoors! Move from outdoors into a building or car with a roof.

during.text: Tornado warning: go to a basement or interior room away from windows.

source.name: National Weather Service (NOAA) -- What to do During a Tornado

during.quote: If you are in a tornado warning, go to your basement, safe room, or an interior room away from windows.

during.text: Protect your head and neck with your arms and blankets.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Tornadoes

during.quote: Protect yourself by covering your head or neck with your arms and putting materials such as furniture and blankets around or on top of you.

during.text: Turn Around, Don't Drown: never drive through flooded roads.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Thunderstorms & Lightning

during.quote: Turn Around. Don’t Drown! Do not drive through flooded roadways. Just six inches of fast-moving water can knock you down, and one foot of moving water can sweep your vehicle away.

during.text: Stay off roads; if trapped in your car, stay inside.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Winter Weather

during.quote: Stay off roads if at all possible. If trapped in your car, then stay inside.

after.text: Watch for fallen power lines and trees; report them immediately.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Thunderstorms & Lightning

after.quote: Watch for fallen power lines and trees. Report them immediately.

after.text: Stay out of damaged buildings; wear sturdy shoes in storm debris.

source.name: National Weather Service (NOAA) -- What to do After a Tornado

after.quote: When walking through storm damage, wear long pants, a long-sleeved shirt, and sturdy shoes. Contact local authorities if you see power lines down. Stay out of damaged buildings.

after.text: Never use a portable generator inside your home or garage.

source.name: National Weather Service (NOAA) -- Caution! Winter Storm Dangers Linger

after.quote: Never use a portable generator inside your home or garage.

after.text: Keep listening for warnings; more rounds of storms may follow.

source.name: National Weather Service (NOAA) -- What to do After a Tornado

after.quote: Continue to listen to local news or a NOAA Weather Radio to stay updated about tornado watches and warnings. Multiple rounds of thunderstorms capable of producing tornadoes are possible during severe weather outbreaks.

before.text: Learn to recognize the signs of heat illnesses.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Extreme Heat

before.quote: Learn to recognize the signs of heat illnesses

before.text: Identify places to get cool, like libraries and shopping malls.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Extreme Heat

before.quote: Identify places in your community where you can go to get cool such as libraries and shopping malls or contact your local health department to find cooling options in your area.

before.text: Do not rely on a fan as your primary cooling device.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Extreme Heat

before.quote: Do not rely on a fan as your primary cooling device. Fans create air flow and a false sense of comfort, but do not reduce body temperature or prevent heat-related illnesses.

before.text: Cover windows with drapes or shades.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Extreme Heat

before.quote: Cover windows with drapes or shades.

during.text: Never leave people or pets in a closed car.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Extreme Heat

during.quote: Never leave people or pets in a closed car on a warm day.

during.text: No air conditioning at home? Go to a cooling center.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Extreme Heat

during.quote: If air conditioning is not available in your home find a cooling center.

during.text: Drink plenty of fluids to stay hydrated.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Extreme Heat

during.quote: Drink plenty of fluids to stay hydrated.

during.text: Avoid high-energy activities and outdoor work during midday heat.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Extreme Heat

during.quote: Avoid high-energy activities or outdoor work during midday heat if possible.

after.text: Heat stroke is an emergency: call emergency services or go to hospital.

source.name: National Weather Service (NOAA) -- Heat Cramps, Exhaustion, Stroke

after.quote: Call 911 or get the victim to a hospital immediately. Heat stroke is a severe medical emergency. Delay can be fatal.
after.note: The NWS heat illness page is not split by phase; its first aid applies whenever symptoms appear (during or after the heat). 911 generalized to 'emergency services'. Confirm the phase placement.

after.text: Move heat stroke victims to cool shade and apply cold, wet cloths.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Extreme Heat

after.quote: If possible, move the person suffering from heat stroke into a cool, shaded area. Remove any outer clothing. Place a cold, wet cloth or ice pack on the head, neck, armpits, and groin.
after.note: Ready.gov's heat page has no 'after' section; this comes from its 'Heat-Related Illnesses' section, which applies whenever symptoms appear. Confirm the phase placement.

after.text: With heat cramps or exhaustion, go somewhere cooler and sip water.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Extreme Heat

after.quote: If you have signs of heat cramps or heat exhaustion, go to a cooler location and cool down by removing excess clothing and taking sips of sports drinks or water.
after.note: Ready.gov's heat page has no 'after' section; this comes from its 'Heat-Related Illnesses' section, which applies whenever symptoms appear. Confirm the phase placement.

before.text: Make a household plan, including pets, for where to go.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Landslides & Debris Flow

before.quote: Make a plan for your household, including your pets, so that you and your family know what to do and where to go in the event of a landslide.

before.text: Leave if told to evacuate or if staying home feels unsafe.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Landslides & Debris Flow

before.quote: Leave if you have been told to evacuate or you feel it is unsafe to remain in your home.

before.text: Near a wildfire burn area, get alerts and watch weather forecasts.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Landslides & Debris Flow

before.quote: If you are near a wildfire burn area, sign up for emergency alerts and pay attention to weather forecasts for the burn area.

before.text: Listen and watch for rushing water, mud or unusual sounds.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Landslides & Debris Flow

before.quote: Listen and watch for rushing water, mud or unusual sounds.

during.text: Stay alert and awake in storms; many landslide deaths happen during sleep.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Landslides & Debris Flow

during.quote: Stay alert and awake during a storm that could cause a landslide. Many deaths from landslides occur while people are sleeping.

during.text: In a landslide's path, move uphill as quickly as possible.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Landslides & Debris Flow

during.quote: If you do get stuck in the path of a landslide move uphill as quickly as possible.

during.text: Never cross a road with water or mud flowing.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Landslides & Debris Flow

during.quote: Be aware that by the time you are sure a debris flow is coming, it will be too late to get away safely. Never cross a road with water or mud flowing.

during.text: Near streams, watch for sudden flow changes or water turning muddy.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Landslides & Debris Flow

during.quote: If you are near a stream or channel, be alert for any sudden increase or decrease in water flow or water that changes from clear to muddy. These can be signs that a landslide is coming.

after.text: Stay away from the slide area; more slides may follow.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Landslides & Debris Flow

after.quote: Stay away from the slide area. There may be danger coming from additional slides.

after.text: Watch for flooding, which sometimes follows landslides and debris flows.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Landslides & Debris Flow

after.quote: Watch for flooding. Floods sometimes follow landslides and debris flows because they may both be started by the same conditions.

after.text: Check for injured or trapped people without entering the slide; direct rescuers.

source.name: Ready.gov (FEMA) -- Landslides & Debris Flow

after.quote: Check for injured and trapped persons near the slide, without entering the direct slide area. Direct rescuers to their locations.

after.text: Report broken utility lines and damaged roads or railways to authorities.
